name: Nureum · 누름꽃
description:
Nureum (누름꽃, meaning “pressed flower”) is a quiet, offline-first iOS app that turns flowers found in everyday life into digital pressed-flower keepsakes.

Photograph a flower in the camera tab—or choose one from Photos—and Nureum gently separates it from its surroundings. You can refine the cutout, adjust its pressed texture, fading, warmth, grain, and edges, then preserve it in My Flower Collection with the date, location, notes, and tags attached to the moment.

The collection can be searched and revisited by flower, season, date, or place. A fully localized Guide introduces 355 flowers across eight languages, including their blooming seasons, habitats, characteristics, and traditional flower meanings.

In the decoration tab, saved flowers become creative materials. Arrange them over photographs, move, resize, and rotate them like stickers, then finish the composition with frames, handwriting, and other decorative elements before saving or sharing it.

Nureum also keeps its social layer intentionally small. Pair with one Flower Friend and send a single flower to their private flower inbox through CloudKit. A home-screen widget brings flowers from your collection back into view, while the share extension lets you preserve photographs directly from the Photos app.

There is no separate account to create, no advertising, and no subscription.

Nureum is built for iOS 17 and later with SwiftUI and SwiftData. Its core collection and image-editing experience works offline and processes photographs directly on the device. VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest performs foreground segmentation, while Core Image renders the pressed-flower treatment. SwiftData manages structured metadata, and original photographs and derived assets are stored separately in a file-backed media store to preserve image quality and keep the database lightweight.

CloudKit powers the one-to-one Flower Friend connection and flower delivery. WidgetKit, App Groups, and the share extension allow saved flowers and incoming photographs to move naturally between the app, the home screen, and Photos.
features: Photograph a flower or import one directly from Photos
Create an on-device foreground cutout with Apple Vision
Fine-tune the cutout and pressed-flower treatment non-destructively
Preserve each flower with its date, location, notes, and tags
Search and revisit flowers by season, date, name, or place
Explore a fully localized Guide containing 355 flowers in eight languages
Arrange saved flowers into cards and photographs with frames and decorative elements
Pair with one Flower Friend and send a flower to their private inbox
Revisit flowers through a home-screen widget
Import photographs using the system share extension

name: PickCam
tagline: Auto-reframe any group video around one person
description:
Group dance videos, concerts, school recitals — the moment you actually want is one person, but the frame is everyone. PickCam turns any multi-person video into a fancam of whoever you pick: tap a person once and the app follows them to the end of the clip, reframing every frame around them for 9:16, 1:1, or 16:9. Version 1.2 adds Lock-On, which pins the subject's face, torso, or body center to one spot on screen while the background moves — a look dance editors usually build by hand with point tracking and keyframes.

Everything runs on-device; there is no server and no account, and video never leaves the device. A Core ML person detector (D-FINE-N) works alongside Apple's Vision framework, while a face-embedding model (AuraFace) and full-body appearance features re-identify the chosen subject after occlusions, crossings, scene cuts, and re-entries — the hard part of this problem is not finding people, it's not losing the *right* one. For clips where dancers cross constantly, an optional precision-tracking pack (EdgeTAM video-memory models, about 54 MB) is delivered as Apple-hosted On-Demand Resources, so the app itself stays under 100 MB. On a ground-truth benchmark measured on a real device (group-dance clips labeled once per second), the share of time spent on the right person rose from 40.3% in v1.1 to 72.8% by default, and from 82.7% to 98.9% on the real clips with precision tracking. All bundled weights are Apache-2.0.

Lock-On is split into two passes: a template tracker follows the chosen point every frame, then a layout pass picks the smallest zoom (at most 25%) that keeps the whole person in frame and smooths the crop within the region where it stays inside the source frame — so there are never black bars. In synthetic tests, face jitter in the output fell from 1.39% / 2.46% of frame height with smooth follow to 0.50% / 0.33% with Lock-On. Because layout is separate from tracking, changing the framing re-lays out the path instantly, and the editor preview is exactly what gets exported. Subjects can be switched mid-video with a glide or a cut, and keyframes fix any missed detection. Export runs through AVFoundation with Metal-based upscaling up to 4K, monetized with StoreKit 2 subscriptions and a rewarded-ad, daily-quota free tier. Localized in eight languages.
features: Tap one person in a group video and get a fancam — AI follows them to the end
Lock-On pins the face, torso, or body center to one spot while the background moves, zooming only when needed
Switch to another person mid-video — the camera glides over, or cuts
On-device detection and face re-identification that survives occlusion, crossings, scene cuts, and re-entry
Optional precision-tracking pack for crowded choreography (Apple-hosted On-Demand Resources)
The preview is the export — flip between Result and Original to see the exact crop
Reframe to 9:16, 1:1, or 16:9 and export up to 4K (HEVC/H.264) with Metal-based upscaling
Native on iPhone and iPad, localized in eight languages
